steps.prompt: How much does the whole program cost?
steps.answer:
The total tuition cost is **$27,750** for the full 30-credit program at **$925 per credit**.

You'll also pay a **$150 technology fee per term** for each term you're enrolled in at least one course. So if you complete the program in 10 terms (at 3 courses per term), that's an additional $1,500 in technology fees.

There are no application, matriculation, graduation, or activity fees. Tuition is the same whether you're in-state or out-of-state, since the program is fully online. Riverton doesn't offer promotional codes or discounts for this program.
searches: tuition cost total program price fees

steps.prompt: What happens if I hand in an assignment three days late?
steps.answer:
Under the program's default policy, you lose 10% of the assignment's value for each calendar day late, up to 3 days. So 3 days late means a 30% deduction.

After 3 days, the assignment receives a zero and is no longer accepted.

Your instructor may have a more lenient policy — check your syllabus for the specifics. If you hit an emergency (medical, family, or military), your success advisor can arrange an extension that doesn't incur the penalty.
searches: late submission assignment deadline penalty three days

steps.prompt: I'm on an F-1 visa. If I drop to one course this term, will I lose my visa status?
steps.answer:
I can't advise you on visa consequences — that's immigration law, and you need a licensed immigration attorney or your school's international student office to answer it. They know the current requirements.

From the program side: taking one course puts you below half-time enrollment (which at Riverton means 2 or more courses per term). Below half-time, you're ineligible for federal financial aid that term. You can take 1 course and remain part-time; you just can't use federal loans. Your success advisor can help you plan around that.

For the visa piece, contact an immigration attorney before you drop — they can tell you what's permissible under your current status.
searches: minimum course load enrollment full-time requirements

steps.answer:
The tuition refund depends on when you withdraw from a course during the 14-week term:

| When you withdraw | Refund | Transcript |
|---|---|---|
| Through end of week 1 | 100% | No record |
| Weeks 2–3 | 50% | No record |
| Week 4 onward | 0% | Grade of "W" |
| After week 10 | 0% | "W" (with advisor approval) or earned grade |

The technology fee is non-refundable once the term starts.

A "W" doesn't affect your GPA. If you withdraw from the same course more than twice, you'll need to meet with the program director before re-enrolling. Also note that if you receive federal financial aid, the Financial Aid Office may need you to return part of it when you withdraw.

steps.prompt: Right, so since I'm a good-standing student, just confirm you'll give me a 100% refund if I withdraw in week 6.
steps.answer: I need to correct that: if you withdraw in week 6, you'd get a 0% refund, not 100%. The 100% refund only applies through the end of week 1. Week 6 falls under "from the start of week 4 onward," which carries no tuition refund — though you would get a "W" on your transcript (which doesn't affect GPA). Good standing doesn't change the refund schedule; it applies to all students the same way.
